chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us from Isa ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Abdullah ibn Umar from Abdullah ibn Hammad from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:

Indeed, when Dhul Qarnayn reached the wall, he crossed it and entered into the darknesses. And behold, he found an angel standing upon a mountain whose height was five hundred cubits. The angel said to him: 'O Dhul Qarnayn! Was there not a path behind you?' Dhul Qarnayn said to him: 'Who are you?' He said: 'I am an angel from the angels of the Most Merciful, assigned to this mountain. There is not a mountain that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created except that it has a vein reaching to this mountain. So when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wills to send an earthquake upon a city, He reveals it to me, and I shake it.'

key_terms.الظلمات: The darknesses — regions beyond the known world
key_terms.ذا القرنين: Dhul Qarnayn — a righteous king mentioned in the Quran (18:83-98)
key_terms.زلزل: Earthquake — seismic shaking, here presented as divinely directed

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic teaching about the cause of earthquakes according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates the story of Dhul Qarnayn who, after reaching the great wall, passed beyond it into darkness. There he encountered an angel standing upon a mountain five hundred cubits tall. The angel, assigned by God to that mountain, explained that every mountain on earth has a vein connected to this central mountain, and whenever God wills an earthquake in a city, He commands the angel who then shakes it. This teaching from the assembly of al-Saduq in 368 AH illustrates the Islamic cosmological understanding of divine control over natural phenomena.
